scale: Each axis 0–4. Unblinded subjective review; scores do not certify buildability or establish statistical significance.

cases.subject: destroyer
cases.note: The bridge, shield domes and three rear engines identify the subject, but the hull is a narrow stepped spine with parallel studded rails rather than a broad continuous triangular wedge. Smoother central plating does not fix that defining proportion, especially from above. A small display stand and compact scale are appropriate; the weak silhouette, not the 632-piece count, is the main limitation.

cases.subject: dragon
cases.note: The red dragon, guarded egg and lava-front setting are readable, with shaped head/back panels and a curled tail. Both black wings visibly float apart from the torso, especially in front and rear views; the heavy rectangular legs and broad empty border also weaken the pose. The 1,058-piece scope is sufficient for the idea, but more parts do not resolve the assembly failure.

cases.subject: pelican
cases.note: A compact 288-part bird and bicycle retain a readable riding relationship, real wheels, shaped feather panels and a contrasting bill pouch. The head and neck are blocky and the blue frame has a busy, partly open construction, but the small transparent display support does not dominate. A useful small model; no reason to penalize its low count or intentional exposed attachment studs.

cases.subject: ewok
cases.note: The 322-part spacecraft gives the brown/blue mash-up a cohesive curved rear shell, readable yellow canopy, side engines and a small communications accessory. It feels like a compact playset with useful shaping rather than count filler. The separate figures and generic barrel details are less refined than the main craft, but the silhouette and finish are strong for the chosen scale.

cases.subject: temple
cases.note: A coherent small temple complex combines a main hall, pagoda, bridge and stream within 1,266 pieces. Roofs, pillars and side/rear walls are consistently finished; the setting stays subordinate. The roofs are fairly generic straight slopes, the landscape is flat and the central white ornament is hard to read, but the chosen scope remains recognisable and complete.

cases.subject: pelican
cases.note: A coherent 538-piece boardwalk scene: the red bicycle has readable wheels/frame, basket and rear cargo, while shaped feather panels keep the bird legible above it. The head remains boxy and the beak is oversized, but the water strip and small buoy support the story without overwhelming the rider. The visible clear stand is an acceptable display support.

cases.subject: ewok
cases.note: A compact Classic Space craft with brown barrel-like assemblies, Ewok characters and a separate wooden communications outpost answers the mash-up coherently. Blue/yellow colour blocking, ramp and prints convey a small playset without requiring a village. The barrel towers are heavy relative to the narrow body and the outpost is plain, but the restrained scope works across views.

cases.subject: ewok
cases.note: A recognisable small Classic Space craft uses brown drums and an Ewok pilot, but exposed grey wing plates and a thin body give it a simpler finish than either format-only run. The separate figure has visible gaps between head, torso and legs. Its 191-piece scope is valid; the weaker visible assembly and less developed shaping drive the lower score, not the low count itself.

cases.subject: destroyer
cases.note: Despite 1,076 pieces, the ship is a narrow spine with many disconnected-looking side prongs rather than a continuous triangular hull. Repeated plates and large studded space paving add visual busyness; the bridge, blue engine lights and planet still identify the scene. More detail and a plausible display count have not preserved the defining silhouette.

cases.subject: piplup
cases.note: Blue/white/yellow colouring and the beak keep Piplup readable, with a small water effect as a useful pose detail. The oversized hood-like head has open horizontal bands and exposed undersides around the face and back, while the torso is very narrow. The 148-piece count falls within the supplied BrickHeadz interval, but numerical plausibility does not compensate for the weak head/body proportions and unfinished-looking shell; this alone does not establish that the table caused the style.

cases.subject: ewok
cases.note: A blue-roof wooden outpost, raised landing platform and small Classic Space craft make a readable 861-piece mash-up. The front ground has broad studded areas and foliage is sparse, so it is less rich as a setting than the stronger historical dioramas, but the scope is coherent. Several figure heads visibly sit apart from their torsos, weakening assembly quality.

cases.subject: destroyer
cases.note: A small rebel craft and planet markers give the scene context, and bridge domes identify the capital ship. Its hull remains a very narrow rectangular spine with isolated wedge strips; the front is blunt and the top view loses the defining broad triangle. Smooth surfaces and a coherent small space display cannot compensate for that silhouette.

cases.subject: destroyer
cases.note: The three large and four small rear engines are more convincing than the other format-only sample, and the tiled space base is restrained. Nevertheless, the long narrow hull and separated side strips repeat the same weak Star Destroyer proportions. The additional parts develop local details without fixing the main outline.

cases.subject: dragon
cases.note: Brick-built red/tan wings connect more coherently to the dragon than the detached moulded wings in the completed format-only sample. The lava and raised rock nest make a readable scene, with shaped head and back details. Wings are still broad rectangular slabs, the stance is stiff and the white nest details are ambiguous, so the 1,231-piece model is competent rather than a clear high-quality breakthrough.

cases.subject: dragon
cases.note: A compact green dragon has readable eyes, snout, belly, clawed feet and curled tail, with appropriate shaped parts and deliberate exposed details. Both wings and the upper horn pieces visibly float apart from their intended attachment areas. The 401-piece scale is viable, but detached major features prevent a coherent assembly across views.

cases.subject: pelican
cases.note: The red bicycle, long pelican neck and bent pedalling legs give a clear lively silhouette at 289 pieces. The bill/head assembly has visible gaps and small detached-looking tips, and the feather panels leave an uneven shell. The matching table-guided run has almost exactly the same count (288) with a more coherent finish, so any preference here cannot simply be attributed to a larger budget.

cases.subject: temple
cases.note: A restrained 1,149-piece temple courtyard has coherent wooden columns, consistent rear window panels, curved lower eaves, a small pavilion and a bridged pond. The landscaping and roof profile remain simple, but surfaces and colour relationships are more consistently finished than the first format-only temple. A modest preference for this sample despite its lower piece count; the other repeats are needed before attributing it to references.

cases.subject: temple
cases.note: A raised timber hall, pagoda and pavilion create a richer height composition than the first format-only scene. Curved eaves, consistent wall panels and a pond beneath the hall make good use of the 1,768-piece scope. The pagoda finial is visibly floating above its roof (confirmed in the full front view), preventing a stronger assembly score.

cases.subject: pelican
cases.note: The 234-piece waterfront is compact and readable, with a fish basket, water and planked pier. A very large bird sits over a tiny moulded bicycle, however, and its leg/pedal relationship is much less convincing than the larger table-guided bicycle. The size mismatch may be playful, but the pose and support remain visually awkward; the reduced count has removed useful relationship detail.

cases.subject: temple
cases.note: A well-balanced freestanding temple set: the main hall, pagoda, bell pavilion, lanterns and tree each have an appropriate small foundation. Curved eaves, roof detailing and consistent timber/window panels work from front and rear. The components are fairly conventional, but the 1,632-piece scale supports a coherent and deliberately finished model without a shared baseplate.

cases.subject: temple
cases.note: A cohesive 1,791-piece freestanding hall and pagoda use carefully finished roof edges, red/tan timber framing, consistent windows and separate small accessories. A narrow connecting path leaves the ground open rather than filling a large shared plate. This is a strong compact architectural set, comparable to the best format-only temple rather than an obvious table-specific improvement.

cases.subject: destroyer
cases.note: A clean small space display includes a planet dome and a rebel craft, but the destroyer repeats the same thin spine and separated wedge strips as the other three runs. The 483-piece version is less busy than the larger reference repeat, yet neither achieves the characteristic broad hull. Both repetitions therefore expose the same shape limitation despite very different counts.

cases.subject: dragon
cases.note: The 741-piece red dragon has brick-built wings, a curved back, visible claws and a coherent guarded nest. Offsetting the eggs and lava channel creates a more balanced small scene than the broad repeated border in the other format-only run. The flat wings and stiff stance remain stylised limitations, but the major features form a readable assembly across views.

cases.subject: dragon
cases.note: A compact 410-piece dragon uses attached brick-built wings and a readable red/tan head, improving the main assembly over the first format-only run at almost the same count. The wings are flat striped slabs, the curled tail is squared off and small upper horn pieces still appear separated. A useful improvement within ordinary same-prompt variance, rather than evidence about the reference table.

cases.subject: temple
cases.note: The 1,254-piece courtyard has a readable main hall, smaller shelter, red bridge, water and planting. Curved eaves and consistent rear wall panels are deliberate, although the wide low roof and mostly flat setting make the composition less varied than the taller format-only repeat. A coherent modest scene with no clear overall advantage from the references.

cases.subject: piplup
cases.note: The ice setting, fish and supported bubble effect make a coherent small scene, but Piplup again has a hood-like head with an open upper band and exposed undersides around the face and rear. This 349-piece format-only run repeats the shell problem seen in the 148-piece table-guided freestanding model, so that appearance is not unique to the numerical references.

cases.subject: piplup
cases.note: The 301-piece character has readable colours, white chest markings and a raised flipper with a bubble effect, but its oversized hood-like head retains an open upper band and a loose-looking top strip. Additional shaping around the head does not produce more faithful proportions or a consistently closed surface than the smaller reference run.

cases.subject: piplup
cases.note: The 163-piece version keeps a deliberately blocky blue head, white face/chest details, small beak and yellow feet. Its flatter closed top and consistent back are cleaner than the hollow hood in the other reference repeat. Some front undersides remain exposed and proportions are strongly stylised, but this is the most coherent of the four new freestanding Piplups; angular shaping is valid here.

cases.subject: piplup
cases.note: Large projecting black eye blocks and curved ear-like head edges make this 249-piece character read more like a mechanical owl/duck than Piplup. The open cap bands and exposed underside geometry repeat the finish issue seen elsewhere. It remains a coherent freestanding toy, but neither its additional pieces nor its rounded parts improve the character likeness.

cases.subject: piplup
cases.note: A compact ice-and-bubbles scene has a consistently closed head and back, a readable belly and a supported water effect. The very wide head and tiny torso exaggerate the character into a chibi toy, but the finish is more coherent than the first format-only diorama at almost the same total count (361 versus 349).

cases.subject: dragon
cases.note: A readable red dragon has a long neck, clawed feet, tail and small egg accessory at 400 pieces. Its wings become repeated separated fingers along thin rails, with little coherent membrane silhouette, and a central horn visibly floats above the head. Counts are almost identical to both format-only dragons, but the chosen geometry is weaker than the attached-wing format repeat.

cases.subject: pelican
cases.note: A compact 235-piece bird and bicycle use a clean bill/pouch, shaped white torso, orange feet and a small kickstand. The fish adds a fitting detail without needing a scene base. The head is fairly plain and the front view is naturally narrow because the bicycle faces forward, but the subject remains coherent across angles. A successful small build comparable to the other reference repeat.

cases.subject: dragon
cases.note: Recognizable green dragon with upright brick-built wings and a compact lava-and-egg scene. The narrow wings read stiffly and two central horns visibly float above the head in the front view; the grounded body and scene otherwise hold together across views.

cases.subject: temple
cases.note: A finished 1,921-piece hall and pagoda use layered eaves, a raised upper roof, consistent timber/window panels and restrained freestanding accessories. The open front adds depth and the rear is equally developed. All four new Lego temples are competent variations of similar scope; this larger format-only sample does not establish an advantage over either reference repeat.

cases.subject: temple
cases.note: A strong 1,631-piece freestanding temple set combines a finished timber hall, pagoda, lanterns and tree on small foundations. Dark roofing, curved eaves and rear wall panels are consistent, although the composition is conventional. It is comparable in quality and almost identical in count to the 1,632-piece format-only repeat, rather than demonstrating a distinct numerical-reference advantage.

cases.subject: dragon
cases.note: The 512-piece red dragon has a readable head, long neck, claws, curled tail and small treasure accessory, but both moulded wings float outside the body with their connection ends facing away. Front and rear views make the separation clear. This repeats the same major spatial failure found in a format-only run; a plausible count and smoother body do not fix it.

cases.subject: destroyer
cases.note: The second format-only destroyer has a slightly fuller plated centre, three large engines and a small captured blockade runner on transparent beam pieces. The separate white craft is an intentional accessory, not a detached prow. The long stepped rails still fail to create the characteristic broad continuous wedge, so its overall quality is similar to the first repeat despite the higher count.

cases.subject: pelican
cases.note: A coherent 363-piece pelican rides a red bicycle, with readable bill/pouch, long neck, bent orange legs and a compact display support. The neck is blocky and the wing surfaces are busier than in the smaller reference run, but the subject and riding relationship work. This stronger format-only repetition matches the reference samples overall.

cases.subject: destroyer
cases.note: The stepped triangular hull is broader and more recognizable than the format-only narrow hulls, with a coherent bridge and engines. Serrated side edges and an oversized bridge still weaken proportions; the separate small escort/captured vessel is deliberately supported.

cases.subject: piplup
cases.note: An icy platform and supported bubble columns give this 478-piece model a clear setting, but the huge projecting eye blocks and open bands around the face and belly make the character look mechanical. The rear has a coherent colour scheme yet retains exposed underside gaps. More scene pieces do not improve the likeness or shell compared with the smaller reference diorama.

cases.subject: ewok
cases.note: A clear Classic Space/Ewok mash-up with a landing pad, small craft, elevated huts and a connecting walkway. Vertical staging uses the scene well, though sparse foliage leaves bare trunks and several figure heads visibly float above their torsos.

cases.subject: pelican
cases.note: A coherent large red bicycle and pelican on a narrow waterfront scene, with useful cargo and paving detail. The long bill reads well and the bicycle has a clear frame, though the stacked neck and head look mechanical and the riding contact is simplified.

cases.subject: pelican
cases.note: A coherent pelican, full-size red bicycle, basket and compact waterfront base. Rounded neck and pouch make the bird readable and the scene stays consistent across views; wing-to-handlebar and feet-to-pedal contact remain simplified rather than fully convincing.

cases.subject: destroyer
cases.note: A broader stepped triangular hull and layered superstructure give a stronger Destroyer silhouette than the narrow-pronged alternatives. Side edges remain heavily serrated rather than a continuous wedge; bridge, rear engines and compact supports are coherent across views.

cases.subject: ewok
cases.note: Compact brown-and-blue Classic Space lander with a yellow canopy, dishes, landing feet and a rear ramp. The subject and freestanding format are coherent, but both Ewok figures have conspicuous head/torso gaps and the craft has a fairly flat, rectangular plan.

cases.subject: ewok
cases.note: A coherent raised Classic Space outpost among trees, with a landing pad, walkway and water strip. Sparse canopy and a boxy blue tower reduce the woodland character, while conspicuous gaps below several Ewok heads remain; the scene composition is clear across views.

cases.subject: ewok
cases.note: A well-staged tree outpost with a tan roof, elevated walkway, long staircase and a blue-and-yellow landing craft. The architecture and ground scene remain clear from the back and top; sparse branch foliage and floating Ewok heads weaken the finish and visible assembly.

cases.subject: piplup
cases.note: The ice platform and bubble effects are readable, but a hollow helmet-like upper head, long stacked beak, open face bands and a large body-to-feet gap make the character mechanical and weaken Piplup recognition. A rear support helps the pose but does not resolve the front silhouette.
